incident-bot: [P1] Elevated 5xx rate detected on /v1/generate (model-runner-prod). Spike started ~2026-03-15T10:02:00Z. 5m error rate: 19%. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/inference-5xx. Pager: maya (oncall).

maya (oncall): I'm on. Initial look: graphs show error spike across us-west-2 and eu-west-1, but us-east-1 is clean.

juan (eng-runtime): grabbing logs from the model-runner fleet now. Suspect: segfaults from the native kernel module when sequence_len > 1024.

priya (eng-infra): I'm checking node events + OOM kills. Running: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --selector=app=model-runner`.

simon (sre): Can we corral affected customers? Dana, any pager/customer-reports?

dana (support): Received two customer tickets for increased 5xx and timeouts, both on long-context requests. Customer A reported timeouts at 10:05, Customer B at 10:07. I told them we're investigating and will update in 15.

juan (eng-runtime): tail from one crashed pod: ```
[2026-03-15T10:04:12Z] model_runner[pid:2345] SIGSEGV at 0x7fffa12b
[2026-03-15T10:04:13Z] GPU driver: Xid 31, context info: fatal error
[2026-03-15T10:04:14Z] coredump saved /var/crash/model_runner.2345.core
```

maya (oncall): That's consistent. Are these all the same model variant?

juan (eng-runtime): Yes — `redwood/gptx-13b-v2` on top of mixed-precision kernels. Crash pattern correlates with kv-cache growth on long-context requests.

priya (eng-infra): Node events show `kubelet` OOM killer invoked on one host yesterday but not recently. No mass eviction. I can isolate the failing pods to a subset of GPU hosts and cordon them.

maya (oncall): Temp mitigation plan: 1) Reroute new requests away from affected hosts 2) Enable fallback to quantized-8bit variant `gptx-13b-8q` for the route 3) Restart crashed pods with `--no-fast-math` to test stability. Who owns applying the route change?

juan (eng-runtime): I can flip the route to `gptx-13b-8q` for `/v1/generate` in the routing layer, for sessions that exceed 512 tokens. Pushing config now.

ops-bot: config-change: routing.v1.generate.fallback_variant -> redwood/gptx-13b-8q by juan at 2026-03-15T10:12:03Z :gear:

maya (oncall): Good. Priya, start draining affected GPU nodes and cordon to stop new pods landing. We want to avoid further crashes while we gather cores.

priya (eng-infra): Cordon + drain in progress for nodes: gpu-az1-07, gpu-az1-09. `kubectl cordon gpu-az1-07` issued.

juan (eng-runtime): I've enabled extended logging and set `CORE_PATTERN` to capture core uploads to S3: `echo /s3/cores/%e.%p.%t > /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern`. Collecting coredumps to s3://rdw-core-dumps/1765432100/ for analysis.

simon (sre): We should also enable a short-term autoscale of the fallback pool to absorb traffic — otherwise latency spikes when variant is slower. Priya, can you bump min replicas for the 8q pool?

priya (eng-infra): Scaling `gptx-13b-8q` pool from 4 -> 12 now. Patch applied.

dana (support): Updated both customers: temporary fallback to a slightly smaller quantized variant is in place, reduced capacity risk, ETA for more updates 30m. Customer A acknowledged.

maya (oncall): Monitoring error rate. Initial drop from 19% -> 6% after routing change but latency up ~120ms. Still seeing isolated segfaults on older hosts.

juan (eng-runtime): Found a suspicious commit in the runtime's custom kernels that changed pointer alignment in attention fusion. Rollback candidate: `release/runtime-kernels@2026-03-10`. Would prefer to hotfix with kernel config first.

maya (oncall): Do we need to roll forward or back? What's safer short term?

juan (eng-runtime): Short term: disable the fused attention kernel on the affected machines (env var `REDWOOD_USE_FUSED_ATTENTION=0`) and restart pods. That avoids touching model weights and is reversible. I'll push a nodeSelector patch to set the env var for new pods on the affected nodes.

ops-bot: deploy: model-runner env update `REDWOOD_USE_FUSED_ATTENTION=0` by juan at 2026-03-15T10:28:40Z :rocket:

priya (eng-infra): Restarted 8 pods on cordoned nodes with the new env. Observability: crashes stopped on those pods.

maya (oncall): Error rate now 2.1% across clusters. Still non-zero, but trending down. We should keep fallback routing for 1 hour and keep min replicas up.

dana (support): Notified Customer A and B that we've applied mitigations and will follow up with details postmortem. Customer A wants ETA for full revert to original variant; said they can tolerate fallback for 3 hours.

simon (sre): Action items logged: 1) collect and analyze coredumps 2) reproduce locally with long-context load 3) prepare kernel-fusion rollback PR 4) run extended soak test on a canary host.

maya (oncall): Handoff to night oncall at 2026-03-15T11:00Z if stable. Who will draft the interim status for executives?

juan (eng-runtime): I'll draft a short exec note with current impact, mitigations, and next steps.

priya (eng-infra): Leaving cordons in place until we confirm no regressions. Scaling and routing kept as-is.

maya (oncall): Great. Summary for the thread: root cause suspected: fused attention kernel regression causing segfaults under large KV growth -> pod crashes -> 5xx spike. Mitigations: reroute heavy contexts to `gptx-13b-8q`, disable fused kernel on affected hosts, cordon/drain nodes, scale fallback pool, collect cores. Customer comms in progress. Postmortem owners: juan/priya/simon.

incident-bot: Incident severity remains P1. Next automated update in 15m.

maya (oncall): I'll update the incident channel and set a follow-up meeting at 11:15 to review coredumps and decide rollback/forward plan.

[end of thread]
